records.name: Vygantė
records.facts_used: Vygantė: The Lithuanian two-stem name is the feminine counterpart of Vygantas. In Antanas Salys’s list of name elements, Vy- is connected with vyti and vyčioti, to chase, while Gant- is referred to Gin(t)-, from ginti, to defend; Vygantas is listed with this second element. These comparisons explain the stems; they are not a single translation of the whole name. Antanas Pakerys’s 2011 study of the accentuation of Lithuanian compound female names, page 94, lists Vygantà, Výganta and Výgantė beside masculine Výgantas. This is dated scholarly evidence for the exact form and its accent. It is not a first registration or the date the name was created.
records.reason: Exact-form or explicitly scoped evidence opened this round supports two paragraphs in five languages; uncertainty kept explicit.
records.uncertainties: Salys 1983 visually checked: PDF 297 / printed 282 Vy-: vyti, vyčioti; PDF 287 / printed 272 Gant-: see gin-, with Vygantas; PDF 289 / printed 274 Gin(t)-: ginti. Pakerys 2011 PDF 5 / printed 94 visually checked: -gant- Vygantà (3a), Výganta (1), Výgantė (1) (plg. Výgantas). Pakerys cites Salys R II 262 for Výgantė, but Salys printed p. 262 (PDF 277) shows Vygandė and Vygintė, not Vygantė; that citation was not used.

records.name: Skomantas
records.facts_used: Skomantas: The Lithuanian name guide explains the two-stem name through sko-, linked with skototis, to care or strive, and mant-, linked with mantus, clever, or manta, property. The explanations of the second element remain alternatives rather than one exact translation of the whole name. Salys’s 1983 volume lists Skomantas as both a personal name and a surname. According to the Universal Lithuanian Encyclopaedia, Skomantas, called Skomond in Old Russian, was a Lithuanian or Yotvingian leader who raided the Pinsk area with Barutis around 1244–1245 and was killed after an ambush. The Galician–Volhynian Chronicle described him as a notable priest and soothsayer. This is a medieval bearer, not proof of the name’s literal meaning or of every modern bearer’s inspiration.
records.reason: Exact-form or explicitly scoped evidence opened this round supports two paragraphs in five languages; uncertainty kept explicit.
records.uncertainties: Exact guide: sko- = skototis (rūpintis, stengtis), mant- = mantus or manta (alternatives kept). Salys PDF 266 / printed 251 Skomantas PN and FN; PDF 317 calendar 27 November Skomantas (Skomas), both from earlier rounds. New: VLE Skomantas article, Old Russian Skomond, c. 1244–1245 raid with Barutis to the Pinsk area, killed; Galician–Volhynian Chronicle calls him a notable priest and soothsayer; Lithuanian/Yotvingian identity disputed. The article gives no etymology; sko- has no Salys element entry, so it stays a guide explanation.

records.name: Astra
records.facts_used: Astra: Behind the Name explains Astra as meaning star, ultimately from Greek astēr, and notes that it has been used only rarely, since the twentieth century. Leili Kuusk’s Estonian name column derives it either from the name of the Greek justice goddess Astraia or directly from aster, star; Astraia itself comes from the same Greek word. The two routes therefore share the star root and differ only on whether the mythological name intervened. The November 2005 issue of Leole, the Suure-Jaani municipal newspaper, uses the exact form Astra in that name column on page 6. This is a dated example from Estonian local print. It is not the first Estonian bearer or proof that every family chose the name for the same reason.
records.reason: Exact-form or explicitly scoped evidence opened this round supports two paragraphs in five languages; uncertainty kept explicit.
records.uncertainties: New: INT-BTN Astra (star, ultimately Greek astēr; rarely used, only since the twentieth century) and Astraea (Latinized Astraia, from astēr). EE-LEOLE05 PDF 6 visually checked: Astra from the name of the Greek justice goddess Astraia or from Greek aster, star. Both routes share the astēr root; the text keeps the mythological intermediary as an open question.
